approach: Use the authors' released repository as-is: clone it, pip install -e . from requirements.txt, ignore the UTF-16 environment.yml and the R/rpy2 comparison tests, and run examples/randu.py under the Agg backend to confirm the published Figure 1 demo. Add one thin reproduce.py that executes the author example unchanged, then repeats the exact Section 3 three-line fit with X = generate_randu(), ICS(S1='cov', S2='tcovAxis', algorithm='standard') and fit_transform, alongside a PCA baseline on the same data. It saves a side-by-side component plot and a gap-cluster diagnostic for the last invariant component, records C1 as a 1/0 structural indicator per A8/A3, and also inventories the four algorithms and eight scatters for C2/C3. All results are written to results/metrics.json and no author source file is modified.

files.purpose: Thin full-release wrapper: run authors' examples/randu.py unchanged, then perform the exact Section 3 RANDU ICS fit and PCA baseline, save diagnostic figure, run C2/C3 and cheap requirement inventory checks, and write results/metrics.json. No author code is edited.

config.install: git clone https://github.com/cbecquart/ICSpyLab; python -m pip install -e . from the clone using requirements.txt
ignore: environment.yml (UTF-16 encoded, conda/R pins; do not use)
tests/comparisons/test_python_vs_r.py (requires R/rpy2; not needed for C1)
config.randu_generator: icspylab.distributions.generate_randu() with package defaults; do not override n/seed unless the generator requires arguments (A2)
config.standardization: none; pass X=generate_randu() directly to fit_transform (A6)
config.component_order: use the package-returned column order exactly as in X_ics=ics.fit_transform(X); A3 assumes ascending generalized kurtosis with the extremal component last, but reproduce.py must not manually reorder the package output

tcovAxis_args.location: fixed at the sample mean of the observation pairs
tcovAxis_args.initialization: sample covariance scaled to unit determinant

config.sign_convention: leave solver signs; judge structure up to axis reflection (A7)

C1_structural_proxy.method: sort the 1D projected values, form gaps between consecutive sorted values, cluster where a gap exceeds gap_factor times the median within-level gap, and count clusters with at least 1% of points
C1_structural_proxy.note: audit proxy only; the saved figure is the primary qualitative evidence per A8. Do not tune thresholds to force a pass.

plot.panels: ICS pairwise scatter matrix, PCA pairwise scatter matrix, and histograms of the last invariant component vs PCA components (A9)

config.random_seed: package RANDU default; numpy seed 0 only for any auxiliary ordering/checks

steps: Clone the public repository if it is not already present: git clone https://github.com/cbecquart/ICSpyLab and cd into it.
Set up only the Python environment: python -m pip install -U pip, then python -m pip install -e . from the clone. Do not use environment.yml and do not install rpy2/R or run the R comparison tests.
Run a quick import check: import icspylab, numpy, scipy, sklearn, numba; confirm the installed package version is 1.0.2 and matplotlib can use Agg.
Run the authors' demonstration unchanged: MPLBACKEND=Agg python examples/randu.py. Confirm it exits 0 and generates the RANDU ICS/PCA panels.

Create results/ and write reproduce.py. In reproduce.py, first execute the author example unchanged with runpy.run_path('examples/randu.py', run_name='__main__') after setting MPLBACKEND=Agg, so the entrypoint still runs the authors' script.

In reproduce.py, repeat the exact Section 3 data flow for numeric evidence: X = generate_randu(); ics = ICS(S1='cov', S2='tcovAxis', algorithm='standard'); X_ics = ics.fit_transform(X); pca = PCA(n_components=3, svd_solver='full', random_state=0); X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X).

In reproduce.py, verify both outputs are shape (n,3) and finite. Compute the gap-cluster diagnostic for the last column of X_ics and for each PCA column; save a diagnostic figure showing the ICS pair matrix, PCA pair matrix, and histograms of the last IC vs PCA components to results/randu_ics_vs_pca.png.

Set C1 value=1 only if the last invariant component shows the RANDU parallel-hyperplane banding under the documented qualitative/proxy check and PCA components do not; otherwise value=0. Record the proxy diagnostics, figure path, and any ordering ambiguity from A3 in metrics.json.

Run C2/C3 inventories: fit ICS on the same RANDU data for each algorithm in ['eigh','standard','whiten','QR'] and record successes; use each scatter name in ['cov','covW','cov4','covAxis','mcd','tcov','tcovAxis','tM'] as an S1/S2 specifier and record successes. C2 value is the number of usable algorithms; C3 value is the number of usable built-in scatters.

Run cheap requirement checks where possible: R1 BaseEstimator inheritance and fit/transform/fit_transform methods; R2 constructor parameters S1/S2/algorithm/component selection; R5 ComponentSelect median/normal/unimodality importable and omission allowed; R6 Scatter base class importable; R7 static source check for numba/njit in tcov/tcovAxis; R8 static source check for sklearn MinCovDet in mcd; R9 generate_randu import/use; R10 distribution generators importable; R11 LICENSE.txt contains MIT and repository URL.

Run MPLBACKEND=Agg python reproduce.py from the repository root. Inspect results/randu_ics_vs_pca.png once; if the proxy and the figure disagree, document the discrepancy and use the figure as the primary C1 evidence per A8. Write results/metrics.json with C1, C2, C3, and requirement-check statuses.
Do not modify any file under icspylab/ or examples/. If an author script fails only because of display blocking, rerun with MPLBACKEND=Agg; do not patch the script.
smoke_test:
MPLBACKEND=Agg python - <<'PY'
from icspylab.distributions import generate_randu
from icspylab import ICS
X = generate_randu()
ics = ICS(S1='cov', S2='tcovAxis', algorithm='standard')
Z = ics.fit_transform(X[:200])
print(X.shape, Z.shape, Z.shape[1] == 3)
print('finite:', bool(__import__('numpy').isfinite(Z).all()))
PY
Expected: X has shape (n,3), Z has shape (200,3), finite=True. First tcovAxis call may take a few seconds for Numba compilation.
intermediate_checks: Package import succeeds on Python 3.12: import icspylab, numpy, scipy, sklearn, numba; no R/rpy2 needed.
generate_randu() returns a 2D array with shape (n,3), n at least several hundred, all values finite, and no constant/degenerate columns.
ICS(S1='cov', S2='tcovAxis', algorithm='standard').fit_transform(X) returns shape (n,3), finite, and has a well-defined last column.
PCA(n_components=3).fit_transform(X) returns shape (n,3), finite; use it as the sanity baseline for the absence of banding.
Gap-cluster diagnostic on the last invariant component is in the small-cluster regime (2 to 30 clusters) while PCA components are not; if not, inspect the saved figure before assigning C1.
C2 inventory returns exactly the set {'eigh','standard','whiten','QR'} with no fit errors on the RANDU sample; record per-algorithm status.
C3 inventory returns all eight scatters {'cov','covW','cov4','covAxis','mcd','tcov','tcovAxis','tM'} usable as S1/S2 specifiers; record per-scatter status and any wrapper/JIT notes.
R1/R2/R5/R6/R9 import and API checks pass; R7 confirms numba/JIT use for tcov/tcovAxis; R8 confirms mcd uses sklearn MinCovDet; R11 confirms MIT license text and GitHub URL.
No comparison test under tests/comparisons/ is run; environment.yml is never parsed.
budget_plan: Reference budget is about 6 minutes, dominated by installation. Allocate ~3 minutes to clone/pip install -e . and verify imports (Numba wheel may be the slowest part), ~30-60 seconds to the smoke test including first-call Numba compilation, ~1 minute to run examples/randu.py plus the exact ICS/PCA fit and diagnostic plotting, and ~30 seconds to finish inventory checks and write results/metrics.json. Total expected ~5-6 minutes on CPU; no GPU and no R installation are used. If pip install is slower, keep the full run because the actual ICS computation is sub-minute.
